extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) sets out two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometrics), the provider may choose internal control (Annex VI) or notified body assessment (Annex VII), depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied.

Annex VII (notified body) assessment is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI systems; most other high-risk AI systems may use the self-assessment Annex VI route.

For high-risk AI systems already covered by existing EU product-safety legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the conformity assessment procedures under that sectoral legislation, with notified bodies ensuring compliance with the AI-specific requirements as well.
Substantial modification of a high-risk AI system requires a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market.

Under Article 43(1), for the purposes of the conformity assessment under Annex VII, the provider may choose any notified body, except that where the system is to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities or EU institutions/bodies, the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority to authorise, by derogation from Article 43, the placing on the market or putting into service of a specific high-risk AI system for a limited period for exceptional reasons of public security, life/health protection, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets, without the standard conformity assessment.

Article 44 covers certificates issued by notified bodies, Article 45 covers information obligations of notified bodies, Article 47 covers the EU declaration of conformity, and Article 48 covers CE marking, forming part of the broader conformity assessment framework (Section 5 of the Act).

Annex VII, point 4.5, provides that where necessary to assess conformity with Chapter III, Section 2 requirements, and after other reasonable means have been exhausted, the notified body may be granted access to the training and trained models of the AI system, including relevant parameters, subject to intellectual property and confidentiality protections.
Article 43(5) gives the European Commission power to adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to update Annex VI and Annex VII in light of technical progress.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies designated under the AI Act.

A Council document (dated 2026) references an Article 30-based scope of designation for conformity assessment bodies notified under the AI Act, using AIP codes tied to Annex I categories of AI systems.

A Commission document (COM(2025) 836, dated 2025) proposes adding a new Annex XIV to list categories and corresponding types of AI systems for the Commission's NANDO (New Approach Notified and Designated Organisations) information system, and includes amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate the AI Act's high-risk requirements, indicating this notified-body listing framework is still in proposal/legislative stage as of late 2025.
As of late June 2026, zero notified bodies had been designated under the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) in the NANDO database; this is a separate but related EU regulatory regime for notified bodies.

As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem specifically for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across member states, limited capacity, and uncertain timelines, ahead of an August 2026 deadline.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical device AI systems (MDR/IVDR interplay context).

High-risk AI obligations under the AI Act are stated to fully apply from August 2026, after which notified bodies designated under the AI Act are expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments, intersecting with existing MDR/IVDR notified body assessments.

As of October 2025, the NANDO system listed 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies (under the Medical Devices Regulation and In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation, not the AI Act specifically).

The Commission publishes designated notified bodies in the NANDO information system, filterable by legislation, and Article 44(12) of Regulation (EU) 2017/745 and Article 40(12) of Regulation (EU) 2017/746 require Member States to make public summaries of annual monitoring reports on notified bodies.
Notified bodies are independent third-party organisations officially designated by an EU member state to perform conformity assessment procedures.

Commentary interprets that the applicable Article 43 conformity assessment procedure depends on the type of high-risk AI system, with biometric systems under Annex III point 1 potentially using internal control or notified body assessment depending on application of harmonised standards.

A 2022 proposal text of Article 43 (pre-final version, dated 25.11.2022) similarly described that for high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III, providers applying harmonised standards or common specifications could opt for one of the listed conformity assessment procedures, indicating this structure existed in draft form before final adoption.

report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes two main conformity assessment pathways for high-risk AI systems: internal control (Annex VI) and notified body assessment (Annex VII), with the applicable route depending on the system's category ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [Powerquant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment)). However, the notified body infrastructure required to implement Annex VII assessments appears substantially incomplete, with no source confirming any specific bodies formally designated under the AI Act as of late 2025/2026, creating significant uncertainty as the August 2026 high-risk compliance deadline approaches ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [mdxcro.com](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 of the AI Act sets out two routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). For systems listed in Annex III, point 1 (biometrics), providers may choose between internal control and notified body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf)). Some commentary suggests Annex VII assessment is mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems, with most others eligible for self-assessment (low confidence) ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

For high-risk AI systems already covered by existing EU product-safety legislation (Annex I, Section A — e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)). Substantial modifications generally trigger a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Under Article 43(1), providers may generally choose any notified body, except where systems are deployed by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority performs the role (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits derogation from standard conformity assessment for limited periods on public security, health, or infrastructure grounds (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). The framework also includes Article 44 (certificates), Article 45 (notified body information obligations), Article 47 (EU declaration of conformity), and Article 48 (CE marking) (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-60)). Annex VII, point 4.5, allows notified bodies access to training and trained models where necessary, subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
Article 35 establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies under the AI Act (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). A 2026 Council document references an Article 30-based designation scope using AIP codes tied to Annex I categories (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). Separately, COM(2025) 836 proposes a new Annex XIV for the NANDO system to list AI Act notified-body categories, indicating this framework remained in legislative proposal stage as of late 2025 (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

By contrast, as of October 2025 NANDO listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies — figures relating to existing sectoral regimes, not the AI Act specifically (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). As of March 2026, the AI Act-specific notified body ecosystem was still being built across member states, with limited capacity ahead of the August 2026 deadline (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated for AI-in-medical-devices assessments (low confidence) ([aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources disagree on the precise designation status: some describe an "ecosystem being built" while others suggest zero designations, without citing an official NANDO count for the AI Act specifically (low confidence throughout). There is also tension between sources treating the NANDO/Annex XIV mechanism as a pending 2025 legislative proposal versus Article 35 being framed as already-adopted law ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35), [Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)). Several claims rated low confidence (0.12–0.24) rely on undated blog sources rather than primary legal text, warranting caution.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source provides an authoritative current count of notified bodies formally designated under the AI Act (as distinct from MDR/IVDR/CRA). It remains unclear whether Annex XIV amendments have been formally adopted, how the August 2026 deadline interacts with apparent designation shortfalls, and which specific high-risk categories require Annex VII versus Annex VI assessment beyond biometrics and sectoral products. No named notified bodies were identified in any source.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes two main conformity assessment pathways for high-risk AI systems: internal control (Annex VI) and notified body assessment (Annex VII), with the applicable route depending on the system's category ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [Powerquant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment)). However, the notified body infrastructure required to implement Annex VII assessments appears substantially incomplete, with no source confirming any specific bodies formally designated under the AI Act as of late 2025/2026, creating significant uncertainty as the August 2026 high-risk compliance deadline approaches ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [mdxcro.com](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 of the AI Act sets out two routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment), [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). For systems listed in Annex III, point 1 (biometrics), providers may choose between internal control and notified body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf)). Some commentary suggests Annex VII assessment is mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems, with most others eligible for self-assessment (low confidence) ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

For high-risk AI systems already covered by existing EU product-safety legislation (Annex I, Section A — e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)). Substantial modifications generally trigger a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Under Article 43(1), providers may generally choose any notified body, except where systems are deployed by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority performs the role (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits derogation from standard conformity assessment for limited periods on public security, health, or infrastructure grounds (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). The framework also includes Article 44 (certificates), Article 45 (notified body information obligations), Article 47 (EU declaration of conformity), and Article 48 (CE marking) (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-60)). Annex VII, point 4.5, allows notified bodies access to training and trained models where necessary, subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
Article 35 establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies under the AI Act (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). A 2026 Council document references an Article 30-based designation scope using AIP codes tied to Annex I categories (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). Separately, COM(2025) 836 proposes a new Annex XIV for the NANDO system to list AI Act notified-body categories, indicating this framework remained in legislative proposal stage as of late 2025 (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

By contrast, as of October 2025 NANDO listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies — figures relating to existing sectoral regimes, not the AI Act specifically (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). As of March 2026, the AI Act-specific notified body ecosystem was still being built across member states, with limited capacity ahead of the August 2026 deadline (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated for AI-in-medical-devices assessments (low confidence) ([aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources disagree on the precise designation status: some describe an "ecosystem being built" while others suggest zero designations, without citing an official NANDO count for the AI Act specifically (low confidence throughout). There is also tension between sources treating the NANDO/Annex XIV mechanism as a pending 2025 legislative proposal versus Article 35 being framed as already-adopted law ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35), [Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)). Several claims rated low confidence (0.12–0.24) rely on undated blog sources rather than primary legal text, warranting caution.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source provides an authoritative current count of notified bodies formally designated under the AI Act (as distinct from MDR/IVDR/CRA). It remains unclear whether Annex XIV amendments have been formally adopted, how the August 2026 deadline interacts with apparent designation shortfalls, and which specific high-risk categories require Annex VII versus Annex VI assessment beyond biometrics and sectoral products. No named notified bodies were identified in any source.
